headers.//: Flutter's bootstrap and service worker are NOT content-hashed, so a cached copy keeps serving the previous build forever. Never cache them; everything they pull in is hashed and safe to cache hard. MUST be the last entry: when two header rules match the same file, Firebase applies them in array order and a later rule overwrites an earlier one's value for the same key — this rule matches *.js too, so if it came first the broad rule below would win instead, which is exactly the bug that shipped (service worker cached 7 days, site stuck on a week-old build).
